label: Faceted browse
description: Three pane faceted browse over a large item set: app sidebar, a fixed-width filter rail of collapsible facet groups, and a result list of composed cards. The defining trait is scale: a live total, per-facet counts, and results that carry their own metadata rather than fitting table columns. Derived from the Studio Catalog page.
when: Use when the user browses or narrows a large collection by several independent facets at once. Do NOT use table-list: a table cannot hold a filter rail, per-facet counts, or a result unit richer than a row. Do NOT use search-filtered-table, which is explicitly the single-search-no-facets case.

slots.rail: Filter rail: a range facet, a counted checkbox facet list, a toggle facet, and type-to-search selects
slots.results-header: Live result total plus a save-this-view action
slots.bulk-bar: Select-all plus batch actions, with the sort control opposite
slots.results: Result cards: type and sharing tags, title and technical name, lifecycle stage and completion, a Data Product / Connection line, summary, property chips, pending-suggestion chip, and last updated

renderNotes: Children of a VERTICAL frame must omit `sizing`. `sizing.horizontal:"FILL"` emits `flex:1`, which in a column container stretches them vertically and distributes the height evenly.
fmSlider and fmProgressBar read the VARIANT (Progress= / Completion=), not props, and collapse to zero width inside a centred row unless hosted in a fixed-width frame.
Use DIVIDER for full-width rules. RECT takes a fixed pixel width and will not span.

The Item facet lists the tenant's item types with their initials and counts, as the capture shows: Data Products (DP, 7), Datasets (Da, 34), Visualizations (Vi, 1), Data Processes (DP, 37), Use Cases (UC, 1), Data Products (DP, 2), Application (Ap, 3), Audit (A, 2), then "View more (7)". The types, their order and the initials are the tenant's data, not a registry fact: the sixth row is a second, differently coloured "Data Products" type. A type with an item-type-tag rule of its own takes its Type; the tenant's custom types (rows 6 to 8) pass Type=Custom and draw as the base tag.

item-type-tag reads props["Show counter"] || props["Show Counter"] (registry kept both spellings across the glossary/catalog fold-in); either one true shows the counter badge, and both default false, so the registry default is off, not on.
checkbox, toggle and dropdown-select-default render no label element at all when Label is the empty string (Task 1.2), which is how a facet row's own TEXT sibling stays the only visible label.
The results-header/bulk-bar leaves (button, checkbox) are authored in ../sections/control-bar.json, spliced in here as the SECTION node above; its own renderNotes carry their deviations.

Each result is ONE search-result-card at App=Studio (#722): the card itself draws the selection checkbox, the item type tag, the Shared tag, the title and technical name, the lifecycle stage tag, the completion bar with its percentage, the "Data Product / Connection" line, the property chips, the pending-suggestion chip, the description ("No summary available" when it is empty), and Last updated, inside one flat row closed by its own bottom rule. So no sibling read-only-tag, no sibling progress-bar-small, and no DIVIDER between results.

The Studio card's type tag is the item-type-tag markup (.ds-item-type-tag--<type>): a type with a rule of its own (Dataset, Data process, Data product, ...) takes its colour, and a tenant's custom type renders as the base tag.

All six results render the Shared tag (search-result-card's Shared prop defaults true), matching every sample row in the capture; the recipe does not model a non-shared result, which would pass Shared: false.
derivedFrom.screenshot is the live Studio Catalog on manufacturing.zeenea.app, captured 2026-09-30 at a 1440px viewport (saved 1370x897). Every label, count and result on this page is the capture's.

No DS-tier slider exists (checked ds-components-authoring.md's vocabulary table): the range facet keeps fmSlider, unreplaced, same as the pre-2.2 capture. tests/recipes-ds-native.test.js names it as the one exception, with that reason (#742).

Studio's card draws the lifecycle stage left of the completion bar ("In Review", "Approved", "Not staged"). `Stage` is the tenant's word, `Stage type` the read-only-tag hue it maps to: In Review = Stage-6 (blue), Approved = Stage-8 (green), Not staged = Stage-1 (the base pill). The dot stays the shared grey: the product tints it per stage, the design system has no per-stage dot. A result with no stage (Customer 360 Profile) passes none. Property values drop the tenant's option emoji (the hourglass, the medal, the check), which are its own data.
The result list has no pagination: the product loads more results as the list scrolls (40 of 118 on first load, no page control).
